As part of our research project on moral uncertainty in social discounting, we conducted an expert survey on questions of population ethics. This [quarto](https://quarto.org/) notebook provides a detailed analysis of the survey results.

## Data cleaning and descriptive statistics
We start by reading the data. As said in our [preregistration](https://osf.io/fx75c), we exclude answers submitted after the closing date of the survey. Here is a random line from the data:
```{python}
import pandas as pd

df = (
  pd.read_csv("data/results/full-basin-export.csv")
  .rename(columns={"created_at": "timestamp"})
  .astype(dtype={"timestamp": pd.DatetimeTZDtype(tz="UTC")})
  .drop(columns=["remote_ip"])  # IP addresses were not collected.
)

# Survey closing date was 22 December 2024 at midnight, Anywhere on Earth. 
# The Anywhere on Earth timezone is 12 hours behind UTC.
closing_date = pd.Timestamp("2024-12-23 12:00:00", tz="UTC")

late_answers = df.query("timestamp > @closing_date")
df = df.query("timestamp <= @closing_date")

df.sample(1)
```
<br>

Excluding `{python} len(late_answers)` late form submissions, we recieved `{python} len(df)` answers. Philosophy was the most represented discipline with 46 answers (71%). Eleven people (17%) said their main discipline was economics. Five people chose "other", and three respondant left this question blank.

```{python}
import altair as alt

discipline_counts = (
    df['discipline']
    .fillna("no answer")
    .value_counts()
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values('count')
    .assign(percentage=lambda x: 100 * x['count'] / sum(x['count']))
)

discipline_counts['label'] = discipline_counts.apply(
    lambda row: f"{row['discipline']} ({row['count']})",
    axis=1
)

alt.Chart(discipline_counts).mark_bar(size=35).encode(
    x=alt.X('count:Q').axis(None),
    color=alt.Color(
        'label', title=None, sort='-x'
    ).legend(
        orient="bottom", symbolType="circle"
    ),
    order=alt.Order('count', sort="descending")
)
```
